chapter_seo_title: Han Li Negotiates a Teleportation Seat in Starfall Hall — RMJI Ch. 517
chapter_meta_description: Han Li ambushes a smuggling team at the crack of dawn, using social pressure and a credible threat to secure a seat to the Outer Star Seas. Chapter 517 of A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality.
og_title: Han Li’s Greatest Weapon Isn’t a Sword — It’s a Civil Request
og_description: Watch Han Li outmaneuver a nervous smuggling group and two Star Palace enforcers without a single spell. The Mortal Stream way.
twitter_title: Han Li casually hijacks a teleportation trip to the Outer Star Seas
twitter_description: No spells. No fighting. Just perfect timing and a terrifyingly polite tone.

lore_anchors.definition: The primary teleportation hub of Heaven Star City, operated by the Star Palace; used for transmitting cultivators to and from the Outer Star Seas under strictly controlled conditions.
The tiered central mountain of Heaven Star City divided into layers; higher layers are more exclusive and secure, with the Starfall Hall located on the forty-ninth layer.
A protective talisman issued to cultivators before using a long-distance teleportation array; without it, the strain of spatial transit can be fatal.
A colloquial term for a cultivator who has reached the absolute peak of Foundation Establishment but has not yet successfully formed a Golden Core.
The vast, dangerous frontier beyond the settled islands of the Inner Star Seas, known for abundant resources, powerful demon beasts, and the strong-preying-on-the-weak rule.
The dominant ruling power over the entire Starfall Sea region, operating enforcement squads, teleportation arrays, and the sacred mountain hierarchy.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn’t Han Li just overpower the group and force his way onto the teleportation array?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because drawing weapons would trigger an alarm and invite the Star Palace enforcers to swarm the hall; a social threat (exposure to the authorities) is far more efficient and safer than physical violence.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the "double the fee" bribe real, or is it a bluff?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is likely real—Han Li has hoarded enough wealth over the years to afford it—but the bribe is secondary to his real winning move: turning a random group member into a scapegoat by "borrowing" their slot, which forces the group and the enforcers to renegotiate on his terms.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What makes this "Institutional Tribulation" different from a normal fight?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In a normal fight, raw power decides the winner. In institutional tribulation, the protagonist wins by understanding the system's rules and pressure points better than the authority figures themselves—Han Li knows the Star Palace is paranoid about security, so his threat to shout is more terrifying than any sword.
